title: DGS Benefits
summary: A polished, content-focused insurance company website built in Next.js, optimized for branding, SEO, and tracking rather than a complex app backend.
description: A Next.js and TypeScript rebuild of the marketing site for an insurance advisory firm with 35+ years in business.

caseStudy.role: Sole software engineer on the second iteration, partnering with the client's marketing consultant.
caseStudy.problem: The original WordPress site looked dated, was hard to find in search, and wasn't structured to support the firm's lead-generation strategy.
approach: Rebuilt the site in Next.js and TypeScript to modernize the brand.
Restructured content and routing around SEO, giving each page a clear, unique URL.
Implemented metadata, Open Graph and Twitter cards, a generated XML sitemap and robots.txt, and Google site verification, with shared defaults at the root layout so every page inherits them.
Aligned engineering milestones with the marketing plan so the launch landed ahead of open enrollment.
outcome: Lighthouse scores of 100 for SEO and Best Practices, 98 for Accessibility, and 95 for Performance on desktop.
Zero layout shift (CLS 0), so content stays put as the page loads.
Since the relaunch, monthly active users have grown from ~300 to 464 (1.2K over 90 days), still up 12.6% month over month (Google Analytics).
